coverage_meaning: Research response coverage, not independent acceptance or runtime pass

records.text: What is the server/daemon-plus-client architecture for a product multiplexer in which many client views attach to one runtime: how are views opened, closed and split without killing the actor behind them, and which process owns actors, PTYs, canonical state and view projection?

How is exactly one fenced input/resize **lease** defined so that one active client owns input and resize while N-1 clients remain passive readers; how does a passive reader request and receive control; and why must focus or attach alone never steal the lease?

What monotonic per-view cursor, snapshot and replay floor does each view carry; how does a late-joining or reconnecting view converge on the same state; and how do `RESET` and an explicit `GAP` resync a view when the requested cursor falls below the replay floor without inventing an event?

How is a slow, stalled or absent client isolated so it cannot block Stop, canonical append or recovery, and what bounded per-view credit, queue high-water and coalescing rule guarantees that, distinguishing presentation coalescing from the non-droppable command, lease, process-exit, termination and canonical-state events?

How does detach and reattach work across terminal loss (window closed, host sleep, SSH drop, terminal crash) including the zero-view state, and how is reattachment proven to restore a view without relaunching a process, model call or effect?

Which rendering approach best achieves non-flicker output — incremental/diff cell or region updates versus bounded full repaint — and under what measured conditions (near-total screen change, resize storms, very wide Unicode frames) is the competing approach cheaper; what is the decisive falsifier for each?

What frame pacing, event batching and input-priority policy keeps typed input responsive while high-throughput output streams, and how is "update only changed cells" reconciled with correctness under partial frames and resizes?

How are stable scrollback and a **follow-mode** affordance defined so that output does not drag a reading user to the bottom, a new-events indicator restores follow mode, and scrollback remains complete even when live presentation samples repetitive deltas?

What Unicode and IME safety contract is required: grapheme-cluster and display-width correctness, combining marks, wide/ambiguous characters, emoji, paste bracketing, IME composition preserved under streaming, and untrusted terminal control sequences kept from becoming UI commands?

What explicit latency and tail budgets should `PERF-010` require — p50/p95/p99 input latency, frame time, canonical-append delay and coalesced/dropped counts — and what numeric thresholds or "unknown until measured" disposition should each carry, given that no measured result exists for Recursion?

What layout concepts make a best-in-class harness-orchestrator TUI: a focused task workspace, agent tabs and split panes, an attention inbox, and on-demand inspectors (Changes, Context, Route, Usage, Details) — and how do these compose over the R-J interaction model without opening graph, telemetry and evidence panes simultaneously by default?

Against the Grok Build Agent Dashboard, Meta Muse Code, OpenCode, Codex TUI and T3 Code, which cells are source-documented, inferred or `unknown`, and which affordances are already existing (attention inbox, persistence, task graph, receipts, worktrees, configurable workflows) rather than novel?

What, if anything, would make Recursion's TUI genuinely define the category — for example the combined contract of multiplexer-bounded views, truthful accepted/delivered/adopted and continuity state, one bounded step lease and `PERF-010`-bounded multi-view cost — and what would falsify each claimed differentiation?

How does the TUI present truthful state as a set of facts rather than one optimistic badge (saved-locally versus accepted versus delivered/applied versus observed outcome versus settled/unresolved; generated/tested/reviewed/accepted/published; compiled/validated/staged/ effective), and how is a replay gap shown as a marker rather than an invented story?

What keybinding model gives full keyboard access with discoverable, named controls, visible non-obscured focus, logical traversal, focus restoration after closing inspectors, and customizable non-conflicting shortcuts?

How is a persistent, discoverable **Stop** affordance provided with its selected Aggressive/Full/Lazy mode and scope visible, without a mouse-only gesture or a timing-sensitive double keypress, and why must Escape not be globally overloaded with destructive cancellation?

What plain-text, high-contrast and reduced-motion modes are required, and how are status changes announced semantically and rate-limited so a screen reader hears important state without reading every streamed token or stealing focus?

Compare the competing multiplexer approaches — an in-process renderer, a local daemon socket with thin clients, and an external multiplexer (tmux, Zellij or OS terminal panes) as the view host — on detach semantics, process-ownership independence, Windows/Linux parity, accessibility, testability and dependency cost. Do not select one.

Compare the wire and encoding choices — bounded framing, backpressure mechanism, cursor identity (`utf8-byte` versus `event`), snapshot format, and JSON/JSONL versus a binary encoding — against the frozen M1B message set. Do not select one.

How does each multiplexer and encoding option interact with the ratified daemon/broker ownership boundary, the one-lease rule and the Windows ConPTY/Job Object and Linux PTY/session/cgroup paths, and what negative trace would eliminate an option before any benchmark?

What is the decisive falsifier for the claim "an external multiplexer can simply be used as the runtime," and what cost or failure (parity, detach semantics, authority, porting effort under D-033) would reverse the preference for a product-owned view layer?

What provider-free fixtures must accept or reject: an N-view soak at 0, 1, 5, 10 and 20 passive views under idle and high-output loads; a slow or stalled client; a disconnect/reconnect; resize storms; huge output; Unicode and IME sequences; and detached actor lifetime — and what is the exact pass/fail predicate for each?

How do the fixtures prove that closing a view detaches rather than kills, that a split or second view adds no inference, indexing or plugin activation, that a slow client cannot block canonical state or Stop, that cursors stay monotonic and every `perf-010` view count respects the canonical-append and memory bounds, and that no view geometry creates a second portfolio executive — using synthetic events only, with no provider call?

The multiplexer architecture defines a server/daemon plus attachable client views, open/close/ split without killing actors, exactly one fenced input/resize lease, N concurrent views with passive readers, monotonic per-view cursors, `RESET`/`GAP` resync, bounded slow-client isolation and detach/reattach across terminal loss including the zero-view state.

Rendering commits to non-flicker incremental/diff updates with a named bounded-full-repaint competing option, frame pacing, stable scrollback, a follow-mode affordance, Unicode/IME safety and explicit p50/p95/p99 input, frame and canonical-append budgets tied to the `PERF-010` 0/1/5/10/20-view matrix; the canonical append precedes any coalescing or drop.

The TUI section defines the focused task workspace, agent tabs/splits, attention inbox and on-demand inspectors, and its comparison covers Grok Build Agent Dashboard, Meta Muse Code, OpenCode, Codex TUI and T3 Code with per-cell evidence classes (source-documented, inferred or `unknown`), separating genuine differentiation from already existing behavior.

Keyboard and accessibility cover full keyboard access, a discoverable persistent Stop with its Aggressive/Full/Lazy mode visible, no globally destructive Escape, a keybinding model, plain-text/high-contrast/reduced-motion modes and rate-limited screen-reader status announcements.

The open multiplexer decision compares an in-process renderer, a local daemon socket and an external multiplexer (tmux/Zellij/OS panes), and the bounded-framing, backpressure, cursor-identity and encoding choices, with a competing option, decisive falsifier and non-proof for each, and selects none of them.

The provider-free fixture suite specifies pass/fail predicates for the N-view soak at 0, 1, 5, 10 and 20 views, a slow client, disconnect/reconnect, resize storms, huge output, Unicode/IME and detached actor lifetime, and no fixture requires a provider call.

Every recommendation names a competing option, a decisive falsifier and what it does not prove; no language, store, framework, runtime, transport, UI toolkit, renderer, multiplexer, wire encoding or vendor is selected and no route is qualified.

The candidate explicitly states what it does not establish: no measured performance advantage, no route qualification, no entitlement, no UI conformance, no security boundary between views and no measured porting cost.
Protected paths are untouched; privacy and secret scan are clean.
